title: Lamb Rogan Josh
subtitle: Kashmiri braised lamb in a deep red sauce
excerpt: Rogan josh is a slow-braised lamb curry from Kashmir, known for its deep brick-red colour and warm aromatic spicing. The sauce comes from Kashmiri dried chillies and yoghurt rather than fresh tomatoes. This is weekend cooking -- the braise takes time, but the result is exceptional.
sourceNotes: Rogan josh has Persian roots and came to Kashmir with the Mughal court. The word rogan means clarified fat in Persian, and josh means heat or passion. Traditional Kashmiri versions use no onion -- the colour comes entirely from dried Kashmiri chillies.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Cool completely before freezing. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The curry tastes better the next day as the spices mellow. Make up to 2 days ahead and reheat gently.

content.text: Buy lamb shoulder on the bone if you can -- it gives more flavour to the sauce. Boneless shoulder works too. The key step is browning the meat in batches so it colours properly rather than steaming.

items.prepNote: use Kashmiri chilli powder if available
use 4 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed

content.text: Heat the oil in a heavy casserole or cast-iron pot over high heat. Brown the lamb pieces in batches -- do not crowd the pan. Each batch should take 3 to 4 minutes to develop a dark crust. Set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the same pot and cook for 12 minutes until deeply golden. Stir often.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the cardamom pods, cloves, and cinnamon. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the paprika, cumin, coriander, and salt. Stir well. Add the yoghurt one tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly so it does not split.
Return the browned lamb to the pot. Pour in the stock. Bring to the boil, then reduce heat to very low. Cover and braise for 75 minutes until the lamb is completely tender.
Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes to reduce the sauce to a thick coating consistency. Stir in the garam masala.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving. Serve with basmati rice or naan.

items.cause: Added too quickly to a pan that was too hot
items.fix: Add it slowly, one tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly over medium -- not high -- heat

items.cause: The heat was too high, causing the meat to seize
items.fix: Add a little more stock, cover, and continue cooking on the lowest heat for another 20 minutes
Remove the lid and simmer on medium heat until it reduces to your liking

content.text: Rogan josh is the most celebrated dish of Kashmir, cooked in both Hindu Pandit and Muslim traditions -- though the spice blends differ. The Pandit version avoids onion and garlic, using asafoetida instead. The version here follows the broader subcontinental restaurant tradition that has made rogan josh one of the best-known Indian dishes worldwide.
